_comment: THE TECHNIQUE TABLE — one authority, two emitted mirrors.
Generated by `npm run scratch:generate`, gated by `npm run scratch:check`:
-> slengine/generated/sl_scratch_table.inc   (the engine EXECUTES it)
-> web/src/blocks/scratchTechniques.ts       (the UI NAMES it)
Never edit either output. The codebase has a standing law against
hand-mirrored tables (generateTrackParams.ts's header: a mis-mapped field is
written into the WRONG parameter, which is worse than one not carried at
all), and a C table and a TS table describing the same eleven figures is
exactly that shape.
SOURCE: docs/specs/scratching.md §2, which is OUR OWN ENCODING of publicly
documented behaviour from the Turntablist Transcription Methodology plus the
KTH measurements. Nothing here is transcribed from any booklet's figures and
no DJ-software source was read (§7). Reference material stays outside the
repo at ~/reference/scratching/.
THE MODEL, and why it is a rest state plus EXCURSIONS rather than a list of
on/off events. TTM: a click is 'the break in the sound caused by the closing
and opening of the fader in as little time as possible' — a MOMENTARY CLOSE,
not a toggle. So on an open-rest fader a click dips it, and on a closed-rest
fader (transformer, chirp) the same field means a momentary OPEN. One list,
both polarities, no second concept.
PHANTOM CLICKS ARE NOT IN `clicks`. They emerge from the reversal and were
measured at -48 dB / 7 ms on the existing scrub path (sl_tape_scratch_test).
Authoring one would double it.
FIELDS
strokeRest   rest state per stroke: [forward, backward]. Generalises the
spec's `faderRest`, which cannot express the forward/cut (open
on the push, closed on the pull).
clicks       excursions from rest. `stroke`: which half they fall on —
this is the ONLY thing separating a flare from an orbit,
per §2's own Notes column. `at`: position in [0,1) within
that stroke.
clickWidthMs MILLISECONDS, not a fraction. A hand moves a crossfader at a
speed that does not care what the tempo is; measured clicks
run 30-70 ms end to end. Period is musical, width is not.
strokeShape  NEVER triangle. Measured pitch span within one tone averages
2109 cents (>1.5 octaves), so the record velocity is not
constant within a stroke and a constant-rate ramp is wrong.
span         fraction of the loop the gesture covers. SMALL: chirps used
only the first 20 degrees of a 144-degree sample.
periodBeats  one full back-and-forth, in BEATS. Crossfader IOIs cluster on
1/32, 1/16 and 1/8 and record strokes are dominated by 1/8,
so a beat-grid representation is a description of what DJs do
rather than an approximation of it. 0.5 = one 1/8 pair.
NOT IN THE TABLE, and it is a gap on purpose: MILITARY. §2 calls it 'forward
scratches interspersed with rubs' — a CHAIN of two figures at phrase level,
not a figure. TTM notes adjacent open-fader scratches share their boundary
symbols, so chaining is a real feature and belongs to whatever sequences
these, not to an entry here that would have to lie about being one shape.

techniques.label: baby
techniques.hint: the reference case — pure record hand, every break is a phantom click

techniques.label: scribble
techniques.hint: a tremor, not a stroke — very fast, tiny span

techniques.label: forward
techniques.hint: the cut — only the push sounds, the pull is silent

techniques.label: stab
techniques.hint: a fast push at high pitch; the re-cue is not heard

techniques.label: chirp
techniques.hint: closes directly after the gesture starts — one tone per stroke

techniques.label: transformer
techniques.hint: rest closed, several openings across the stroke — many tones per stroke

techniques.label: flare · 1
techniques.hint: one real click mid-stroke, plus its phantom — so it sounds like two

techniques.label: flare · 2
techniques.hint: the canonical case: 2 real + 2 phantom, so it sounds like four

techniques.label: crab
techniques.hint: four rapid clicks — thumb against four fingers; audio-wise a 4-click flare

techniques.label: orbit
techniques.hint: a flare that continues on BOTH strokes rather than one
